question: A product has a marked price of ₹1,200. If a 20% discount is applied, what is the selling price?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount 20% → Ratio of MP : SP = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

5 units = ₹1,200

1 unit = 1,200 ÷ 5 = ₹240

4 units = 4 × 240 = ₹960

**∴ The correct answer is ₹960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹1,200

Discount Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − (Discount% × MP)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d11ef5f8e7390fa6ddaeaa34d7a9759dfbf67c3c0f5d686e45c59df134dca575.png] 

⇒ Discount = 20% of 1,200

⇒ Discount = (20 ÷ 100) × 1,200

⇒ Discount = 0.2 × 1,200 = 240

⇒ Selling Price = 1,200 − 240

⇒ Selling Price = 960

**∴ The correct answer is ₹960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

Also known as the List Price, it is the price printed on the label of an article.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price unless otherwise specified. Discount = MP − SP.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%.
